t: The Ottoman Empire grew from a frontier beylik in Anatolia into a power spanning three continents for over six centuries.
Janissary infantry, gunpowder artillery and a sophisticated bureaucracy let it take Constantinople and rule a diverse realm.
Lost wars, nationalist revolts and European debt control eroded it; defeat in the First World War ended the sultanate in 1922.
dyk: The architect Mimar Sinan is credited with more than three hundred buildings, including the Süleymaniye Mosque in Istanbul and the Selimiye Mosque in Edirne.
ev: Osman I defeats a Byzantine force at the Battle of Bapheus
Orhan captures Bursa, the dynasty's first true capital
Mehmed II captures Constantinople after a siege of some fifty-three days
Selim I conquers the Mamluk Sultanate, gaining Egypt, Syria and the holy cities
Suleiman the Magnificent destroys the Hungarian royal army at Mohács
Jan III Sobieski routs the Ottoman army at the second siege of Vienna
The Tanzimat reforms begin to modernise administration and law
The Grand National Assembly abolishes the sultanate
